title: End-to-End Multi-View Fusion for 3D Object Detection in LiDAR Point Clouds (MVF / dynamic voxelization CoRL 2019)
text: Dynamic voxelization keeps every point and the point-to-voxel and voxel-to-point maps: no cap per voxel, no zero padding, no random drop; hard voxelization (VoxelNet / PointPillars) reserves 100 or more points per voxel and drops by random sampling. Same detector, only the voxelization changed (Waymo vehicle 3D AP 56.62 -> 59.29, BEV AP 75.57 -> 77.18; pedestrian 59.25 -> 60.83; KITTI car moderate 74.7 -> 77.86), latency 41.1 -> 41.1 ms vehicle, 36.1 -> 34.7 ms pedestrian. The fraction of points dropped by hard voxelization is not reported. Page read as ar5iv text (checked).
idea: lossless point-to-cell grouping by index and rank; pooled cell feature handed back to each point

title: BEV-MAE: Bird's Eye View Masked Autoencoders for Point Cloud Pre-training in Autonomous Driving Scenarios (AAAI 2024)
text: BEV-guided masking of whole BEV cells; decoder is one 3x3 conv with two linear heads: 20 points per masked cell as offsets from the cell centre (Chamfer) and the point density (Smooth-L1). Waymo 20 percent labels CenterPoint L2 mAP/APH: scratch 65.60/63.21, coordinates only 66.20/63.71, coordinates + density 66.70/64.25; nuScenes test 71.7 NDS / 67.0 mAP vs 70.2 / 65.5 for TransFusion-L. 38 h for 30 epochs on 8 P40; BEV masking 4.1 GB vs 12.6 GB for voxel masking. Lidar, masked prediction, not self-reconstruction; checked on the HTML page.
idea: K slots of offsets per BEV cell + a count/density head

title: R2LDM: An Efficient 4D Radar Super-Resolution Framework Leveraging Diffusion Model
text: Stage 1: a voxel feature encoder maps radar points to a latent grid; the decoder predicts an occupancy mask and an offset per voxel (P = (centre + offset) * mask) with mask BCE 0.9 + offset L1 0.1; only the average position of the points of a voxel is reconstructed. Stage 2: latent voxel diffusion to the lidar-like target (40.1 M parameters, 128 steps, 9 h + 21 h on an RTX 2080Ti, inference time not reported). VoD CD 0.64 vs 7.36 (R2DM), F-score 0.43 vs 0.08; registration recall 25.6 -> 57.3 percent. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: mask + offset per cell decoder; stage 1 alone as an auxiliary autoencoder

title: Diffusion-Based Point Cloud Super-Resolution for mmWave Radar Data (Radar-diffusion ICRA 2024)
text: Radar points of 5 frames aggregated by relative pose into a 256 x 256 BEV image (height as grey value); mean-reverting-SDE diffusion gives a denser lidar-like image. VoD: RadarHD CD 0.34 / MHD 0.24 -> 0.19 / 0.10; on the RadarHD data set it is worse in CD (0.44 -> 0.59). One RTX 4090 for 9 h; inference time not reported. The numbers set the scale (0.2-0.4 m) of radar-to-lidar point reconstruction, they do not test self-reconstruction. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: one-directional Chamfer / Hausdorff for how many real points are recovered

title: ALSO: Automotive Lidar Self-supervision by Occupancy estimation (CVPR 2023)
text: Pretext task: a 4-layer MLP (128 units) takes the latent of a support point and the offset of a query and outputs occupancy; queries in front of / behind a lidar return and on the sight line, BCE. nuScenes mIoU MinkUNet 0.1 / 1 / 10 / 100 percent labels 21.6 / 35.0 / 57.3 / 71.2 -> 26.2 / 37.4 / 59.0 / 71.8; KITTI moderate R40 SECOND 65.35 -> 68.07, PV-RCNN 70.57 -> 72.53; one 16 GB V100. Gain fades with labels; radar would need other labels. Checked (HTML up to character 100,000).
idea: continuous-offset query decoder as a training-only reconstruction head
licence: open source licence not named on the page

title: Convolutional Occupancy Networks (ECCV 2020)
text: Per-point PointNet features are average-pooled onto planes or a volume, a U-Net processes the grid, a small MLP decodes occupancy at any query by bi/trilinear interpolation. ShapeNet 3-plane 64^2 IoU 0.884 / Chamfer-L1 0.044 / F-score 0.942 vs global-latent ONet 0.761 / 0.087 / 0.785; rooms 64^3 volume IoU 0.849 vs 0.475; bilinear 0.805 vs nearest 0.766; volume 32^3 -> 64^3 0.782 -> 0.849. Runtime not on the page. Shows a mean-pooled grid decodes well when the per-point MLP runs before the pooling and the query is continuous. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: grid encode + continuous-query decode; regress attributes of the nearest detection as a probe
licence: not stated on the page (memory MIT; to check)

title: Deep Set Prediction Networks (DSPN NeurIPS 2019)
text: Set decoding by gradient descent on a learnable set so that its encoding matches the target latent; avoids the responsibility problem of MLP slots. MNIST auto-encoding Chamfer x1e-3 0.09 vs MLP 0.21 vs RNN 0.49; CLEVR AP95 85.7 vs 57.9 (evaluation bug noted by the authors); T = 10 steps cost about 75 percent more training time. States that Chamfer gives loss 0 for {a,a,b} vs {a,b,b} (blind to multiplicity) and that Hungarian is one-to-one at O(n^3). Checked on ar5iv.
idea: Chamfer cannot see duplicates: add a count term; exhaustive permutation min for K <= 4

title: Objects as Points (CenterNet)
text: Heat-map peak at stride 4 plus an L1 sub-cell offset head (weight 1, evaluated only at keypoints) that recovers the rounding error. COCO: 614 pairs of 860,001 objects share a centre cell at stride 4 (<0.1 percent cannot be predicted); with ground-truth heat-map, size and offset about 0.5 percent of objects are still missed (discretisation and Gaussian rendering). The only collision statistic found; it does not transfer to radar returns in a 0.5 m cell, which has to be measured. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: cell + offset code as the decodable position representation

title: PointRNN: Point Recurrent Neural Network for Moving Point Cloud Processing
text: State = point coordinates + a per-point state tensor; old and new points are paired by kNN or ball query on coordinates, the update concatenates the own feature, the neighbour state and the displacement, shared FC + max pool; GRU / LSTM variants. Future point prediction CD / EMD: nuScenes 0.0619 / 0.3750, Argoverse 0.2789 / 0.8964; Moving MNIST 2 digits PointLSTM 5.18 / 4.21 (ball query beats kNN); 49.6 GFLOPs vs 345 GFLOPs for a voxel ConvLSTM. Lidar-scale clouds, prediction task, no detection or map result. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: history kept as aligned points with a state; raster built once

title: RV-FuseNet: Range View Based Fusion of Time-Series LiDAR Data for Joint 3D Object Detection and Motion Forecasting
text: Past sweeps are ego-aligned and merged in the range view; early (warp all to the latest view) vs late vs incremental (fuse sweep by sweep, small viewpoint steps). nuScenes AP at 0.7 / L2 at 3 s: 57.9 / 135 cm, 58.8 / 127 cm, 59.9 / 120 cm. States that information loss and gaps grow with ego and actor speed. No cost comparison. Evidence that many small alignment steps beat one big one; the winning variant passes features, not points. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: sweep-by-sweep recurrent update with small steps

title: Semantic-Supervised Spatial-Temporal Fusion for LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection (ST-Fusion)
text: CenterPoint on nuScenes val mAP / NDS: single frame 57.28 / 65.58, data fusion (points concatenated, time lag attribute) 58.86 / 66.43, feature fusion 59.79 / 67.48, ST-Fusion 60.48 / 68.32. Data fusion NDS by number of frames: 65.58 / 66.19 / 66.43 / 66.07 for k = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, so it saturates at 4. Authors blame object motion; no ego or Doppler correction described; no latency. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: point accumulation alone saturates; number of sweeps has an optimum

title: ALICE-LRI: A General Method for Lossless Range Image Generation for Spinning LiDAR Sensors without Calibration Metadata
text: Infers the beam layout, angular distribution and per-beam corrections from the cloud itself so that every point has its own range-image pixel; zero points lost on all of KITTI and DurLAR (abstract page only; no equations, no code). Conventional projection is many-to-one (digest from a search summary). Principle: invertible iff injective plus a stored residual.
idea: invertibility of a sensor-grid image = injective cell assignment + stored residual

title: On the Limitations of Representing Functions on Sets
text: Continuous sum-decomposition rho(sum phi(x)) of permutation-invariant functions on sets of at most M scalars works through R^M (Thm 4.4) and not through R^N with N < M in general (Thm 4.1); similar for max-pooling. Scalars only; toy median experiment shows the useful latent size grows about linearly with M but below M. Argument for K explicit slots instead of one pooled vector per cell. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: pooled cell vector must be as wide as the set it must hold

title: VoxelNet: End-to-End Learning for Point Cloud Based 3D Object Detection
text: Voxels with more than T points are randomly sub-sampled (T = 35 car, 45 pedestrian / cyclist); at most K non-empty voxels are kept; more than 90 percent of voxels are empty; voxel coordinates are hash keys so a point is inserted in O(1) and dropped if its voxel is full (buffers built in one pass). 225 ms on a TitanX of which 170 ms in the 3D middle convs. The origin of the capped per-cell list. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: capped per-cell list as the lossy baseline
extract: skip: row only (facts used in the MVF note)

title: Occupancy-MAE: Self-supervised Pre-training Large-scale LiDAR Point Clouds with Masked Occupancy Autoencoders (first posted as Voxel-MAE)
text: Range-aware random masking of occupied voxels (90 / 70 / 50 percent for 0-30 / 30-50 / over 50 m); the decoder reconstructs only the binary occupancy of each voxel, focal loss, no coordinates; KITTI car 3D moderate 72.55 -> 72.87, cyclist 52.08 -> 54.84; Waymo vehicle L1 AP SECOND 72.27 -> 73.68 with all data; nuScenes 3-frame +1.8 mAP / +1.4 NDS (CenterPoint), single frame +0.5 mAP; about half of the car labels match full-data scratch. No cost figures. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: range-dependent masking ratio

title: GD-MAE: Generative Decoder for MAE Pre-training on LiDAR Point Clouds (CVPR 2023)
text: Reconstruction target: the points of each masked token (at most 64) in token-local coordinates, L2 Chamfer; the generative decoder takes 3.2 ms vs 27.1 ms for a transformer decoder baseline. Waymo mAPH L2 with / without pre-training: 5 percent labels 59.97 -> 63.86, 20 percent 65.35 -> 67.14, 100 percent 67.34 -> 67.64; ONCE mAP 62.62 -> 64.92. No GPU hours. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: local-coordinate point targets per token

title: UniPAD: A Universal Pre-training Paradigm for Autonomous Driving (CVPR 2024)
text: Masked lidar / multi-view inputs lifted to a voxel volume, SDF rendering of depth and RGB along sampled rays, weighted L1 (both weights 10). nuScenes val NDS UVTR-L 67.7 -> 70.6, UVTR-C 45.0 -> 47.4, UVTR-M 70.2 -> 73.2; SpUNet 73.3 -> 79.4 mIoU. Depth-aware ray sampling 32.9 NDS at 1x memory vs 32.5 random and 31.9 dilated. No code link on the page. Rendering is a camera-side idea; checked on the HTML page.
idea: rendering loss for a volume

title: MAELi: Masked Autoencoder for Large-Scale LiDAR Point Clouds (WACV 2024)
text: Abstract page only: masking tied to the sensor's spherical projection and a reconstruction that separates empty space from occluded space (the sensor-blind-spot idea); no numbers or loss form on the page read. Relevant to radar because most of a radar scene is not observed.
idea: separate empty from unobserved space in the reconstruction loss

title: Masked Autoencoder for Self-Supervised Pre-training on Lidar Point Clouds (Voxel-MAE Hess et al.)
text: Digest from a search summary: reconstructs masked voxels and classifies empty vs non-empty; nuScenes +1.75 mAP / +1.05 NDS; 40 percent of the labels with pre-training beat a randomly initialised model. Not opened.

title: VoxelContext-Net: An Octree based Framework for Point Cloud Compression
text: Octree occupancy symbols of non-leaf nodes are coded losslessly with a context network; the distortion comes only from the octree depth (quantisation) and a coordinate refinement module predicts offsets at the decoder. SemanticKITTI saves 31.15 percent bitrate vs G-PCC (OctSqueeze 2.13 percent), 55.51 dB at 0.36 bpp vs 54.35 dB at 0.52 bpp; decoding 52-90 ms on a 2080Ti, 2.15 M parameters. Compression coder, not a feature encoder. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: occupancy code + decoder-side offset refinement

title: OctSqueeze: Octree-Structured Entropy Model for LiDAR Compression (CVPR 2020)
text: Octree with a learned entropy model of the occupancy byte given the ancestors; loss only from the leaf depth (12-16 levels). KITTI example 43.67 PSNR at 1.52 vs Draco 39.09 at 2.04; downstream NorthAmerica detection AP 86.17 at 3.39 vs 85.27 at 5.00 (Draco); encode 49.6-106 ms, decode 166-902 ms on a GTX 1080. Examples are hand-picked. Checked on the supplement via ar5iv.

title: Sparse Tensor-based Multiscale Representation for Point Cloud Geometry Compression (SparsePCGC)
text: Multiscale sparse tensors, per-scale occupancy probability on the most probable occupied voxels (SOPA, SLNE); claims state of the art in lossless and lossy mode on 8iVFB / Owlii / MUVB / KITTI / Ford; no bpp numbers or code link on the abstract page.

title: 4D Spatio-Temporal ConvNets: Minkowski Convolutional Neural Networks
text: Sparse tensor = coordinate matrix C + feature matrix F (COO); quantisation (Alg. 1) sorts and reduces by key and keeps ONE representative index per voxel, so the other points of the voxel are dropped (labels in conflict set to ignore). Generalised sparse convolution on arbitrary output coordinates; 4D net adds under 6.4 percent parameters. Hash-based sparse tensors are lossless only if the quantised coordinates are unique. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: sparse tensor with unique coordinates; duplicates lost at quantisation

title: Voxel Set Transformer: A Set-to-Set Approach to 3D Object Detection from Point Clouds (VoxSeT CVPR 2022)
text: Abstract page: self-attention inside each voxel through two cross-attentions with a few learned latent codes, so voxels of arbitrary size are handled in parallel at linear cost; competitive on KITTI and Waymo; a search summary states that it avoids the stochastic point dropout of equal-sized grouping (digest). No latency on the page. Per-cell set encoder without a cap.
idea: per-cell latent-code attention for variable-size cells

title: FoldingNet: Point Cloud Auto-Encoder via Deep Grid Deformation
text: Decoder warps a fixed 2025-point (45 x 45) grid concatenated with a 512-d code through two 3-layer MLPs to the point cloud (about 1.05 M parameters, 7 percent of a fully connected decoder); extended Chamfer (max of the two directions). ModelNet40 Chamfer test loss 0.0296 (2 folds) / 0.0290 (3 folds). Global-code decoder, not cell-aligned. Checked on ar5iv.
code: licence at merl.com (terms not on the page)

title: Learning Representations and Generative Models for 3D Point Clouds (Achlioptas et al.)
text: Chamfer vs EMD as autoencoder training loss: the EMD-trained AE gives better generative results and CD is cheaper; CD 'fails to distinguish' samples that overpopulate a region. Chair AE: MMD-CD 0.0004 / 0.0012 (train / test) with the CD-trained AE, MMD-EMD 0.068 / 0.075; EMD-trained 0.0005 / 0.0013 and 0.042 / 0.052; 2048 points, bottleneck 128. Checked on ar5iv.

title: High Resolution Point Clouds from mmWave Radar (RadarHD ICRA 2023)
text: 64 x 256 polar heat-map of 40 stacked frames, asymmetric U-Net to a 512 x 256 lidar-style image, BCE + Dice, threshold to points. Median Chamfer 0.36 m / MHD 0.24 m in the training environment (3.5x and 2.7x better than CFAR), 0.8 / 0.75 m and 1.03 / 0.94 m in two unseen environments. No code URL on the page. Checked on ar5iv and the abstract page.

title: UniFusion: Unified Multi-view Fusion Transformer for Spatial-Temporal Representation in Bird's-Eye-View
text: Abstract page only: spatial and temporal fusion in one formulation with learnable temporal weights; claims less information loss than warping fixed-size BEV memories and state of the art map segmentation on nuScenes; no numbers or code on the page. The 'virtual views' idea named in a search summary was not on the page.

title: Hidden Gems: 4D Radar Scene Flow Learning Using Cross-Modal Supervision (CMFlow CVPR 2023)
text: Digest from a search summary: flow split into a rigid ego-motion part (differentiable weighted Kabsch from the first flow estimate) and a residual; static background flow supervised from the radar ego-motion, foreground from tracked boxes; co-located lidar / camera / GPS-INS only as training supervision. Used for motion segmentation and ego-motion. Not opened.
idea: per-point motion = ego part + residual

title: Dual-Weight Particle Filter for Radar-Based Dynamic Bayesian Grid Maps
text: Each particle has a position, a velocity and two weights (position, velocity); the radial velocity is projected into x-y and rewards particles whose velocity matches a nearby measurement. Simulated roads (MATLAB toolbox, 200 m x 25 m at 0.5 m, 10,000 particles): simple road dv 0.39 m/s, dx 0.53 m, tracked 91 percent; highway tracked 63 percent vs 34 / 40 percent. No runtime, no real data, no ego-motion description on the page. Particles move as points, so there is no grid resampling. Checked on ar5iv.

title: Masked-reconstruction self-supervised pre-training on radar point clouds (Takai et al. Kanazawa University JSAE 2026)
text: Digest from a search summary (abstract behind a login): self-supervised pre-training by masked reconstruction on radar point clouds, tested on object detection; no numbers, no data set named. The only radar masked-reconstruction work found; no arXiv version.
